content: {"summary":"Similar memory‑creep and redis‑features latency spikes have occurred before (e.g., incident INC‑0097) and are linked to Redis hitting its maxmemory causing write refusals, which lets the fraud‑scorer feature cache grow unchecked. The usual immediate mitigation is to restart the fraud‑scorer pods before the memory limit is hit and, as a longer‑term stop‑gap, set vm.overcommit_memory=1 to avoid the MISCONF path.","likely_cause":"Redis reaching maxmemory (noeviction policy) triggers MISCONF/OOM paths, causing writes to be refused and the fraud‑scorer in‑process cache to grow unchecked.","confidence":"medium","claims":[{"text":"This issue has happened before, documented in incident INC‑0097 where redis‑features latency spikes caused scorer memory creep.","evidence_ids":["INC-0097#2"],"quote":"If redis-features slows again and the climb returns, restart before the limit, not after."},{"text":"The known cause is the in‑process feature cache growing without bound when redis‑features is slow.","evidence_ids":["RB-006#0"],"quote":"fraud-scorer rss creep. ns `risk`. known cause: in-process feature cache grows without bound when redis-features is slow"},{"text":"The usual stop‑gap is to restart the fraud‑scorer pods before the memory limit is reached.","evidence_ids":["INC-0097#2"],"quote":"If redis-features slows again and the climb returns, restart before the limit, not after."},{"text":"A common mitigation is to set vm.overcommit_memory=1 to avoid the MISCONF path on Redis writes.","evidence_ids":["RB-019#3"],"quote":"ssh redis-features-01.prod.internal 'sudo sysctl -w vm.overcommit_memory=1'"}],"next_checks":["Check Redis INFO memory used_memory vs maxmemory","Verify vm.overcommit_memory setting on redis‑features host","Monitor fraud‑scorer pod memory usage and FRD‑W118 warnings","Consider a rolling restart of fraud‑scorer deployment if latency spikes recur"]}
